I need some help with motivation

Hi all,

So I am vegan for almost 5 years now, and my age is 31. Something I noticed is that during the years 2020-2021, which was around the pandemic, there was a great hype and advertisement around veganism, and cafes were creating many vegan options and similar stuff. Now, it seems very clear that veganism has not taken over the world, and despite being staunchly angry at the very beginning because of the harm animals suffer from, I am feeling nihilistic now about the state of the world. What can I do to remotivate myself in this deeply disturbing world ?

Day 1 of being vegan successful

I decided to go vegan last night for moral, ethical and environmental reasons and so far I’m doing great!

A lot of my favourite foods (anything beige really) are already vegan or can easily be swapped out for a vegan alternative that still tastes good, and the more I get into it the more I’m realising that it’s not about making everything taste the exact same as the non vegan version, all that matters is that it still tastes great and makes me feel good.

I was afraid of vegan milk alternatives that I talked about in my last post but today I got my first vegan chocolate milk and I chose the Oatly one, and I will say at first the initial unusual and unfamiliar oat taste was a bit meh (because I’m not used to it) but the more I drank the more I found I really like it, and it doesn’t make my belly hurt like dairy does so I can drink more of it without ending up with bad stomach ache!

I will say I did not eat healthy today, I went a bit wild and bought a bunch of sweets that are vegan that I already like (fruit mentos, fruit pastilles, jelly tots and vegan Ben and Jerrys) and I had a bit of all of them and >!I’m definitely feeling the consequences brewing (so sorry for that)!< and I feel great because I’m not giving up the vast majority of my favourite comfort foods!

For dinner I had wedges, some bread and some quorn chicken (not real chicken) dippers that my mum bought for me, they tasted exactly like chicken so I went back to the freezer and double checked the ingredients, unfortunately the batter does contain milk and egg that my mum didn’t realise but it’s okay because my dad is vegetarian and my mum likes them so they said they’ll eat them and get me the birds eye veggie dippers tomorrow which are vegan.

I’m finishing my day with my oatly chocolate milk because I have milk with my evening tablets and I feel great.

Not so great physically because of the amount of sugar I have consumed but emotionally, I have secretly wanted to go vegan for a long time since my sister went from vegetarian to vegan in 2019 but I made a lot of excuses, I feel very bad about contributing to the meat and dairy industry for all 20 years of my life but I’m deciding to make the rest of my life as cruelty free as possible for the planet and because I love animals 💚🌏💚

Atthe end of the day, it’s better to stop contributing to harmful practices even if you spent a long time doing that than to continue doing harm, I can still love cows and pigs and sheep and chickens from afar knowing I’m not contributing to their suffering anymore even though I feel too guilty to be around them because of my past eating habits.

How do vegans who buy vegan options from popular fast food chains justify spending money on companies that primarily sell meat?

I keep seeing a lot of tiktok trends of vegans showing their go to fast food choices and it’s places like Taco Bell, Burger King, Chipotle, etc. What is the true difference ethically in buying meat vs a non meat option when your money is still supporting the meat industry? I understand that it’s difficult to avoid spending money at places that aren’t entirely vegan (obviously most of us buy from grocery stores and companies that distribute a range of animal and non animal products) but purposefully spending money at fast food restaurants/giant chains that primarily sell meat seems counterproductive to the cause.

Edit because people are getting mad: I am aware that nobody can be 100% vegan and I never claimed that. I’m asking a genuine question about ethics on a thread about veganism.. I personally can’t justify to myself spending money often at fast food companies that play a significant role in mass factory farming so I don’t spend my money there. I’m not judging you if you do, i’m asking what is the thought process behind it. Thank you to those that provided genuine answers 😊

Watched “Earthlings”. Humans are so cruel.

A year and a half into veganism I watched “Dominion”. I watched it twice so I didn’t forget the torture and cruelty I saw.    
Two years and a few months vegan I heard about “Earthlings” and was surprised I hadn’t seen it before. Ii watched it today. My designated “Vegan Day”.    
It’s a little older, but more thoroughly informational in some areas “Dominion” covers in great detail later. Both are devastatingly truthful and explicit, meant for those who truly want to know what is done to living creatures for human purposes. 

So many times I think “how could anyone see this or know, even partially, what they do to animals, how they suffer, and continue making excuses? 
My family are consumers of animal products and I already alienated much of them when I stopped eating meat five or so years ago.. I got all the responses…”no fish?” “No, that’s meat.”. The conversations are definitely more hostile from some 
than others who might have a financial interest or are concerned about lawsuits from vegan channels they force their falsehoods on. (That’s a personal reference)    
This documentary is so heartfelt and intense in a way that anyone with the capacity to watch this would be moved to change.   
I’m disappointed in myself for any time I cower from response because people are just so hostile.   
**We don’t have time to be quiet vegans!** There is so much suffering and cruelty.   
How could anyone think it’s okay to electrocute a living being or remove teeth and bones without painkillers?    
I just keep asking “how?” “How are we more concerned than they?” How can anyone think it’s ok or feel justified in stomping on a live animals head? Or skinning them alive? Some of the fur animals were still blinking after they removed their skin! 
Even though I know I’m more feeling than most, maybe, there must be something so wrong and desensitized about people that work for these industries and continue consuming these products.    
I’m so naive still in so many ways. This documentary shows them killing dolphins and eating them? I thought they were protected. 
It’s doesn’t make it any better based on what animal they are…is anything sacred? How is this torture and cruelty still happening?    
There are so many intelligent people with ideas for ways to make human life better. Why can’t we do it for animals? 
Editors and rewrites of social media content that use their tools to stifle free speech should be acknowledged as the tyrants they are, included are those who write and support “AgGag” laws. Most of what I write isn’t seen or heard because of them. 
**Reddit is the greatest source of freedom for our vegan community.**    
Do you know what this animal felt before they died to feed, clothe or entertain you? It’s sickening. It’s even more sickening that they don’t care.    
It’s not that they don’t know..they don’t care. Everyone should watch “Earthlings”.

Advice needed: How to handle myself better in conversations with non-vegans?

I've been vegan for at least 7 years and have been getting increasingly fed up with the lack of compassion/consideration non-vegans display towards animals. I wouldn't expect people to do a complete 180 overnight and immediately go vegan just because they know a vegan (I certainly didn't), but I'm sick of cutting people slack when I hear the same tired arguments over and over, not to mention seeing people constantly admit they know it's wrong, but don't want to change. 



Anyway, last weekend I was at a wedding and during dinner a conversation came up to do with eating animals. A person at our table said they're fine eating meat because they've worked at a butcher's and in an abattoir and, anyway, they only get meat from locally-grown sources, so it's fine. *(Not an original point, I know...)* At this point, I grumpily snapped something like "But the animal doesn't want to be killed!", which immediately made everything awkward. The other people very quickly left and I later heard them talking to someone else about it. 

 
I clearly went too far and I know I shouldn't have reacted like this\*, it's not that right that my outburst made everyone uncomfortable. I want to be able to respond in conversations like these in a serious, but non-aggressive, manner. Being realistic, I don't expect I'll actually be able to say anything to change people's minds, but I don't want to come across as some crazy vegan.

 
The whole point of this post is I'm looking for suggestions of people I can watch to see examples of people handling themselves in disagreements with non-vegans (I've heard Earthling Ed is a great example of this), so I can handle myself better. Also, if any of you know of any genuinely good responses, which don't make you seem like a complete ass, then I'm all ears for them too. 

 
Tl;dr: How can I better respond in conversations about veganism/eating animals without losing it? Any good resources? 

 

\*The point of this post isn't to do with how we (as vegans) might not like other people (talking about) eating meat or defending it, nor is it about tiptoeing around other people's feelings. Of course, I'm sick of the BS reasons/mental gymnastics people do to avoid confronting the idea that eating animals is wrong, but I need to conduct myself better in conversations like these

Not sure how to reason with parents!

Hey everyone!   
Il try to keep this short:)

So it's still a while away but I cannot stop worrying about it. I'm a new university student, and I will be going home for the first time in December. Before university, I started eating less meat and thought about the idea of going vegan. The only thing really stopping me was that my family eats a fair bit of meat and my parents cooked majority of my dinners (which usually contained meat). Since I started university and I have had control over my own meals, I have been eating almost entirely vegan (apart from eggs which I am still learning to cut out). It's honestly the best decision I have made, but my parents really don't seem to understand. I'm not saying they don't respect the morals, they actually agree that the meat and dairy industry is insanely problematic and eating less meat is beneficial. However, whenever I mention not eating meat *at all*, they say "I don't see why you have to draw such a fine line in the sand. Eating less meat is definitely good, but it's not a problem to have a piece of meat once or twice a week". I just don't really know what to say to that. 
And another annoying thing is that every time I call them, they always talk about all the good (meat centred) meals they are going to make when I am back. They don't do this out of spite or to tease me or anything but I just don't think they have fully processed the fact that I do not want to eat meat. I just feel awkward telling them yknow? They also have never had to cook for vegans before so I feel like it would be awkward if at every meal I have to cook a separate dish.

If anyone has had a similar experience or some advice, please share :))

They want vegans to shut up and go sit in a corner silently.

How many times have you heard about militant pushy vegans? And how many militant pushy vegans have you actually met?

Would you be silent if someone were kicking a dog next to you? Would you kindly ask them to stop kicking the dog? Or would everybody be better off if society shamed the dog kicker for the terrible things they're doing.

 
It's almost as there are more people pretending to be vegan using this rhetoric in order to continue the horrible things that they do unimpeded.

Too many of them use the excuse that because of pushy vegans they will never go vegan. Which is a pitiful excuse to continue abusing animals. This completely diminishes the sense of urgency that's occurring in regard to animal rights.

 
My vote is, we should be loud. We should be disruptive. We should remind animal abusers exactly why we're angry.

Since 11pm last night when I went to bed around 95 million land animals have been killed along with billions of aquatic animals.

 
I check everyday for how many animals die during my sleep. This problem is an urgent one, and i'm tired of seeing people casually ignore it while telling vegans to shut up and go sit in the corner silently.

Real leather bag as a gift

Hi guys,

Tl,dr at bottom

I recently received a brand new real leather designer bag from my MIL as a birthday present. She does know I'm vegan (so is my fiancé) and they're usually very accommodating — I assume she just didn't think that far.

When I received it my first intuition was "shoot, this looks like real leather..."

But obviously me being a crazy people pleaser (ESPECIALLY when it comes to my in-laws) I didn't say anything or checked the tag.

At home I inspected it and it confirmed my intuition. Funnily enough I love the brand and style and was researching months ago if they had any vegan styles (Kate Spade -> settled on vegan lines by Vivienne Westwood). 

Now I feel bad, because I don't think I'll be able to wear it without feeling ill. I also feel terrible, because it was over $250 and brand new.

Here are the options I'm considering:

• Reselling it on online marketplaces since it's NWT

• Gifting it to a non-vegan friend

• Asking my MIL to return it and ask her for another bag (very scared to do that!!)

Has anyone been in a similar situation? Any advice welcome, thank you!!

Tl; dr: received a brand new designer bag made out of real leather from my MIL, don't know what to do with it.

Cow tongue gave me bad dreams

I saw this video on twitter of someone cooking a cow's tongue and it made me feel really queasy and disturbed.. I think it's because a recognizable body part has so much more identity than a hunk of vague meat. You can look at a cheeseburger or a steak and say it's just 'meat'.... but when you see a tongue, you're forced to think about how that was a once living thing, tortured, long dead, and now having its body cut up and boiled. Absolutely horrific. The color too. I went to bed pretty soon after and I had this dream where my mother brought this chicken into the house, those nice red and white ones, and they wanted to kill it but they were doing it so wrong. My young sister who can be pretty arrogant was going to do it and she was going to just hack a cleaver into the side of its neck and I was really upset about this and I was really going crazy trying to find a way to fix the situation and they were putting me in the position to have to kill the chicken the right way but of course there is no humane way to kill... I don't know what happened with that vignette but later in the dream the family dog was made of chickpeas and I had to slaughter my dog if I wanted chickpeas (not implying that that's what I did in the dream I wouldn't do that.)

I think this is pretty interesting and revealing about my psychology. I've only been vegan for 3 weeks or so now and I always feel confused and in a way bothered by those who say that animals are not food in any way or that they're super repulsed by meat and stuff... It made me question myself and my own empathy and all. I had a hard time feeling the way I saw others saying they did and I just didn't get it. I'm referring to how people say things that imply it is absurd that a human being in any scenario would ever come to eat an animal or when they have stronger feelings on veganism than I.

I think I'm starting to get that though. When you are vegan and never see eating from an animal as an option, it is so easy and intuitive, it would never cross your mind to eat meat, and it becomes completely ridiculous that someone would do so! Why! It's so easy not to! Death is such a deeply horrifying thing and it weighs heavy that it is so commonplace. It makes someone so inhuman to truly not care. The person who slaughters an animal scares me. The slaughtered animal scares me.

I'm glad this is happening for me because recently I have a hard time with empathy. I can logically understand what beliefs and decisions are most empathetic and good but I very rarely feel emotion surrounding such things.

Where does someone with Celiac get sufficient vegan protein if they don’t like tofu/soy proteins?

It’s easy to say, “tough luck, maybe try to prepare tofu correctly.” But you can imagine a world where someone just doesn’t like the texture of tofu, intrinsically. 

Look, if I had celiac, I could easily be vegan, because I love tofu products. 

But for someone with celiac, who can’t eat seitan, who truly despises the taste/texture of tofu, are they out of luck? 

Is the answer, “you better eat tofu, because what’s worse: killing an animal, or making tofu?”

Or is it, “sorry, you might just have to supplement with protein shakes, and get your meaty food fix from lions mane and jackfruit.”

Let’s make this even more difficult: what about someone with celiac who also is ALLERGIC to soy? Now we’ve cut the possibility of soy curls, TVP, soy chunks. What have we left? 

Does this person have an obligation to be vegan?

Animal Welfare and Veganism: Food culture, hunting, pets etc.

I’m beginning to go vegan for ethical reasons regarding animal welfare, and I am increasingly finding the relationship humans have with non-human animals to be disturbing, or at least concerning. Food is such a fundamental part of our lives, and I notice for how much people find a love and passion for it, whether it be in cooking or consumption, people prefer to remain either totally ignorant to its origin, or completely romanticize the process of its acquisition. Even to those who defend acquiring food in a comparatively natural or pastoralistic manner to factory farming are still practicing something that has verifiably demonstrated to cause animals psychological and physical harm. It also makes me question about if having pets is at all adequate at times, when people are sometimes uninterested or possibly incapable of providing adequate to an animal, and their possession is totally to fulfill that desire itself whilst insurance of its quality of life is secondary if a consideration made or fulfilled at all. As to food, the effects, the process of collecting and processing animals solely to consume or commodify them is inconsequential, or it is ceremonialized and worshiped despite in some instances the practical possibility of avoidance or replacement of consumption with alternatives that do not involve animals, their culling, captivity, hunting, or slaughter. The butchering, the hammering, the devouring is a part of the process and continuing to eat without guilt, and perhaps gratitude is the only conceivable option. I realize I have for too long depended on conclusions that prevented me from doing more for non-human animals, and for too long have I done nothing despite having the knowledge and the intuition to recognize that it was wrong and that I am capable of minimizing it, beginning with myself, if not preventing and abolishing it.

Vegan Protein With OCD/ARFID?

Hello, I have been vegan for a month now and have been loving it, but I’m looking over the horizon and I fear I may run into a protein deficiency in the coming months or years.

Currently I’m eating around 45g of protein a day. Although the minimum daily recommendation is 58g for my body weight (165 pounds)

Currently I feel better than I ever have... Tons of energy, I’m more motivated than ever, mentally feel amazing. Not using animals has created this incredibly euphoric state in my mind.

I have two questions…

1. Can I eat below the minimum protein requirement of 0.8g of protein per kilogram of body weight. Has anyone done this over an extended period of time?

2. What can I eat with the following dietary limitations? 

\- I can’t eat peanuts because I have a peanut allergy and avoid ALL nuts.

\- My OCD/ARFID makes it so that if I eat beans, chickpeas, protein shakes (I’ve tried pea, and soy) or edamame/soy I begin violently gagging and throwing up the moment it touches my tongue. (Throwing up is not very nutritious)

Currently my protein sources are… Whole Wheat Bread, Pasta, Broccoli, String Beans, and Peas

In the past I would meet my protein requirements by chugging a glass of high protein cows milk with my nose plugged but obviously that is not vegan and I don’t want to perpetuate the abuse of cows.
